title: Return to Growth: Career Reentry and Reskilling Playbook 2026
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines Redwood’s standard approach for colleagues returning from extended leave (parental leave, sabbatical, medical leave, long-term external assignments) and for employees changing roles who require reskilling and re-provisioning. It centralizes expectations, role-specific ramp plans, tooling and benefits adjustments, and the operational steps People Ops, managers, and IT take to return contributors to productive, supported work.

Scope: Applies to all regular employees and contractors transitioning back to Redwood after >30 days away, and to internal transfers that include a substantive tooling or competency change (e.g., moving into infra, SRE, data, or manager tracks). Does not replace standard new-hire onboarding; it augments it for reentry scenarios.

Principles
- Employee-centered: prioritize psychological safety, clear expectations, and flexible timing.
- Measured ramp: use explicit 30/60/90 milestones with objective signals of progress.
- Role-aware provisioning: grant minimum required access initially, expand after verification.
- Manager + People Ops partnership: shared accountability for timelines and outcomes.

Eligibility and Typical Use Cases
- Parental return (12–26 weeks leave)
- Sabbatical or extended unpaid leave (1–12 months)
- Medical leave followed by phased reentry
- External secondments or long-term project assignments returning to a different team
- Internal role changes that require cross-skilling (IC -> manager, IC -> infra/data/product)

Reentry Pathways (choose one primary pathway)
1) Standard Phased Return (typical parental/sabbatical): 30/60/90 ramp, benefits maintained, toolkit reprovisioned within SLAs.
2) Phased + Upskill (return + new competencies): same as Standard + structured reskilling curriculum and mentor pairing.
3) Role Transition Reboard (internal transfer): transfer checklist + dedicated onboarding buddy + skills validation prior to full access.

Operational SLAs (targets)
- Primary communication acknowledged by manager & People Ops: 2 business days.
- Minimum workspace access (email, Slack, Confluence read): 1 business day after reactivation.
- Developer-level access (GitHub, CI, secrets read): within 3 business days after manager approval.
- Elevated system access (PagerDuty, production consoles): verified gating and granted within 5 business days after training verification.

Reskilling Tracks (examples)
- IC -> Engineering Manager: leadership fundamentals, cycle planning, 1:1 framework, calibration training, shadowing 4 weeks.
- Product Specialist -> Data: SQL fundamentals, internal data catalog orientation, two guided projects, mentor check-ins.
- Backend IC -> Serving Runtime/SRE: kernel concepts primer, infra credential training, controlled hands-on lab environment.

Program Steps (high-level)
1) Pre-return coordination (4–6 weeks before planned return or ASAP after notice)
   - Employee completes Reentry Intent form (People Ops link).
   - Manager documents expected role, provisional scope, and ramp target date.
   - People Ops creates an individualized Reentry Plan and identifies required trainings.
2) Provisioning & access (0–5 business days from official reactivation)
   - IT/Access Portal issues baseline credentials: Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, Confluence.
   - Manager signs off to request elevated access: GitHub org membership, CI pipelines, test environments.
3) First 30 days (focus: orientation & safe first tasks)
   - 30-day check-in (manager + People Ops) to verify access, wellbeing, and first deliverables.
4) 60 days (focus: ramping responsibilities)
   - Skills assessments for reskilling tracks; mentor feedback.
5) 90 days (target: independent contributor level for original scope OR agreed new-skill milestone)

Manager Checklist (actionable)
- Complete Reentry Intent form and share role expectations.
- Draft a 30/60/90 ramp plan with measurable outcomes (see template below).
- Submit access requests via Access Portal within 1 business day of reactivation.
- Schedule weekly 1:1s for first 8 weeks, then adjust cadence.
- Pair the returning employee with a mentor/buddy for at least 12 weeks.
- Plan an explicit leveling/compensation calibration within the first 90 days if role or responsibilities changed.

People Ops Checklist
- Review and approve the Reentry Plan and any benefits adjustments.
- Coordinate reskilling budget (learning credits, instructor time).
- Ensure EHR/benefits status remains accurate and any leave-related windows are tracked.
- Book an onboarding session: Systems refresher + internal tools deep-dive.

IT / Access Owner Checklist
- Pre-provision low-risk access (email, Slack, read access to Confluence).
- Verify identity and MFA via Okta.
- Stage elevated access in two phases: dev/test then prod, gated by manager sign-off and training completion.

30/60/90 Ramp Plan Template (example)
- Role: Senior Backend Engineer (returning from leave)
- 30 days: regain codebase familiarity, merge first small bugfix, Slack channel rejoin, complete security refresher.
- 60 days: own a small feature, complete performance review of feature, pair with peer on release.
- 90 days: lead a minor rollout, demonstrate observability ownership on assigned service, mentor new joiner.

Provisioning Matrix (role -> typical initial access -> expansion triggers)
| Role Type | Initial Access (Day 0–1) | Expanded Access (Day 3–5, gated) | Expansion Trigger |
|-----------|-------------------------|----------------------------------|-------------------|
| Knowledge worker | Email, Slack, Confluence read | GitHub read, Jira edit | Manager approval \u0026 30m systems refresher |
| Developer (IC) | Above + GitHub read | GitHub write, CI token, staging env | Code review + security refresher |
| SRE / Infra | Above + Confluence infra docs | Production console, PagerDuty | Hands-on lab completion + manager verification |
| Manager | Above + team org info | Compensation tools, hiring queues | HR approval + manager training completion |

Note: Access Portal (access.redwood.com) is the single source to request and track access. Use the "Reentry" request tag for expedited routing.

Ticket Templates
- Access request (copy into Access Portal description):
  "Name: <Full name>
  Role: <Target role>
  Return date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
  Required access: [email, slack, confluence-read, github-org, jira-edit]
  Manager approval: <manager-email>
  Comments: Returning from <leave type>. Planned 30/60/90 outcomes attached"

- Training completion confirmation (email to People Ops):
  "Subject: Reentry training complete — <Name>
  Body: Completed: Security refresher (date), Tooling lab (date). Recommended to escalate to production access."

Mentorship and Buddying
- Pair returning employees with a short-term buddy (peer-level) for at least 12 weeks.
- Appoint a mentor (1–2 levels senior) for role-specific coaching for 3–6 months depending on reskilling complexity.

Benefits and Compensation Notes
- Benefits continuity: standard employee benefits remain active for approved leaves up to 12 months per company policy; consult Benefits team for deviations.
- Compensation review: internal transfers or promotions that materially change scope should trigger a leveling calibration within 90 days. Manager submits a Leveling Review via the Compensation Portal with supporting ramp outcomes.

Measurements & Success Criteria
- Time-to-first-meaningful-contribution (target: <= 30 days for standard returns).
- Full tooling parity (target: <= 10 business days).
- Employee satisfaction (People Ops survey at 30 and 90 days; target mean >= 4/5).
- Manager confidence score (post-90-day calibration, target >= 4/5).

Common Scenarios and Guidance
- Returning caregiver requesting part-time schedule: create a written phased schedule and document in the Reentry Plan; discuss expectations for deliverables and meeting attendance.
- Returning with a new role: require a documented skills validation checklist and mentor sign-off before prod access.
- Returning from medical leave with accommodations: partner with People Ops and Security to provision necessary ergonomic or access changes before first day back.

FAQ (short)
Q: Who initiates the process?
A: The employee should notify their manager and People Ops as soon as they know a return date; People Ops will open the Reentry Plan.

Q: How long will it take to get production access?
A: Typically 3–10 business days depending on role and verification steps. High-risk access requires demonstrated training and manager authorization.

Q: What if the returning employee wants to shift teams?
A: Treat as an internal transfer + reboarding. Manager-to-manager agreement + People Ops coordination required.

Escalation Paths
- If provisioning exceeds SLAs, manager escalates to AccessOps (accessops@redwood.com) with subject "Reentry SLA breach: <Name>".
- If employee wellbeing concerns arise, People Ops lead (people-ops@redwood.com) to schedule return-to-work check.
